Chapter 7: The Impact of International Politics — Living in the Crossfire
You know, the world outside North Korea always feels closer than you’d think. News of missile launches, high-stakes summits, and fresh sanctions trickles in—sometimes through official announcements, other times whispered in the hallway.
For people living and working inside the country, international politics isn’t just background noise. It shapes life every single day, sometimes in ways you notice right away, and sometimes in ways you only feel later.
One morning, you walk into the office and something’s different. The air’s just heavier. Overnight, there’s been another round of sanctions. Everyone’s waiting for the fallout. The foreign staff gathers for a quick meeting, sorting through the latest restrictions, trying to predict what’s really going to change. Local colleagues look worried. They’re thinking about job security, and what the future holds for the company—and for their families.
The impact? It’s immediate. Shipments don’t arrive. Bank transfers freeze. Projects hit pause. If you’re part of the foreign team, it’s a sharp reminder: all your hard work can be wiped out by a single headline. And for the locals, the uncertainty cuts even deeper. Many are the only breadwinners for their families, and the thought of layoffs is honestly terrifying.
But in the middle of all this, you’ll find moments of real resilience. Picture a local manager, suddenly short on raw materials. Instead of giving up, she rallies a team and they fan out across the city, hunting for alternatives. Or a group of workers who step forward, volunteering for extra shifts—just determined to keep the factory running, no matter what. The foreign staff does its best to help—offering support, sharing news, and trying to keep spirits up.
Still, the pressure wears everyone down. One night, you spot a colleague sitting by himself, gazing out the window. He sighs and says, “Sometimes I wonder if it’s worth it. We work so hard, and it can all disappear overnight.”
There’s no easy answer to that. Only a sense of shared frustration and exhaustion.
International politics—it’s this powerful force you can’t control. All you can do is weather the storm. For anyone inside North Korea, it’s a daily reminder of just how connected, and how vulnerable, you are to the world outside.
But here’s what you learn: patience, adaptability, and the value of holding onto hope—even when everything feels uncertain.
